payload.text: All five `cmd_*.py` success paths are reachable in isolation; placing the banner call between the last `print` and `return 0` does not change exit codes or side effects.
payload.reason: Confirmed by reading each command's source. Each path is a linear sequence of prints + metadata.update + best-effort metrics + return.

payload.text: The E2E test harness's `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)` captures all stdout produced by the CLI subprocess, including the new banner lines.
payload.reason: Standard subprocess behavior; the existing test assertions on `r.stdout` for `shaping -> planning`, `validating -> followups`, `human_review -> done`, etc. already prove this works.

payload.text: The `lib.cli._stop_banner` module can be imported from each `cmd_*.py` without circular imports because the helper has no dependencies on other `cmd_*.py` modules nor on `lib.transitions` / `lib.metadata`.
payload.reason: The helper only needs `sys` (or just `print`) plus an internal data structure. No transitive imports back into the CLI dispatcher.

payload.text: `validate --init` (line 273 in `cmd_validate.py`) lands the run at `validating`, not `human_review` or `followups`. Adding the banner to the default mode only — not to `--init` — is therefore correct.
payload.reason: The transition target on line 248 is literally `"validating"`.

payload.text: `cmd_plan.py`'s `--init` path (line 154) lands the run at `shaping` (still in shaping). Wait — actually re-reading: `--init` requires status=planning and stages templates; the print at line 153 is the `staged {templates}` message, no state change beyond what `shape`'s default mode already did. The banner is correctly tied only to the final-plan path that lands at `ready` (line 264).
payload.reason: Re-confirmed by reading lines 123-154 vs 156-264 of `cmd_plan.py`.

payload.text: The two pre-existing date-baked snapshot drift failures on master (mentioned in the most recent LOG entries) will not be re-baselined by this run; the test plan only adds NEW assertions and NEW snapshot fixtures.
payload.reason: This is a workbench convention reaffirmed by the auto-merge-on-complete run's LOG; we only own banner-related tests.

payload.text: The order of stdout lines in `cmd_validate.py`'s flat-layout path (`validating -> human_review`, `branch:`, `worktree:`, `audit:`) does not need to change; the banner goes AFTER all four existing lines.
payload.reason: Brief: "Banner is purely additive. The existing transition line and any artifact-path line still print first, in their existing order."

payload.text: A merge-conflict failure path in `cmd_complete.py` already exits via `return fail(str(e), e.exit_code)` (line 119) BEFORE reaching the success print at line 137. The banner call placed after line 140 is therefore guaranteed not to fire on conflict.
payload.reason: Code-read confirmation. The `_CompleteError` raise inside `_do_merge` is caught at line 118 and turned into a `fail(...)` return.

payload.decision: One shared helper module `lib/cli/_stop_banner.py` owns the banner format. Every call site passes only `landing_state` and `run_id`.
payload.rationale: The brief mandates "one source of truth for the banner format" so wording stays in sync across five call sites. A free-function module is the lightest viable design.
payload.alternatives_considered: (a) Inline the banner string in each `cmd_*.py`. (b) Add a `print_stop_banner` method on the `transitions` module. (c) Make it a method on a `Banner` class.
payload.why_not_alternatives: (a) violates the brief's single-source-of-truth requirement and guarantees wording drift. (b) couples runtime stdout to the transition engine, which is supposed to be policy-neutral; the transition engine doesn't know about CLI-level concerns. (c) needless OOP overhead for one pure function.

payload.decision: Banner is plain ASCII, fixed at 60 columns, plain `print()` to stdout. No ANSI escapes, no Unicode.
payload.rationale: Matches existing CLI output style across all `cmd_*.py` files (none of them use color or Unicode). 60-column matches the visual weight of the existing `branch: …` / `worktree: …` / `audit: …` lines and is wide enough for the longest banner line (`agent-workbench complete <run_id>  - accept and merge`, ~58 chars even with a moderate-length run_id).
payload.alternatives_considered: (a) Variable width by terminal size. (b) ANSI color (bold red `STOP`). (c) 80 columns.
payload.why_not_alternatives: (a) tests can't reliably pin variable output; snapshot fragility. (b) color codes don't survive pipes and clutter log captures. (c) longer lines for no readability gain; 60 is enough.

payload.decision: Banner prints only on the actual success path of each command, after the transition is durably recorded.
payload.rationale: Brief AC-5 requires that no banner appears on aborted transitions (e.g. merge conflict, dirty worktree). Placing the call immediately before `return 0` on the success branch — after every existing `print` and `metadata.update` — guarantees this.
payload.alternatives_considered: (a) Use an `atexit` hook based on final state. (b) Inject from `transitions.transition(...)` itself. (c) Wrap the whole `run()` function.
payload.why_not_alternatives: (a) `atexit` is global state, fragile under tests, and would fire even on `--init` paths. (b) couples engine to stdout (same as DR-001's rejection of option b). (c) requires intrusive control-flow change for no benefit over the simple in-line call.

payload.decision: Terminal states (`done`, `abandoned`) omit the "Next moves" block and substitute a "Terminal state." line instead.
payload.rationale: Brief AC-3 says terminal states have no next moves. Printing an empty `Next moves:` block would be visually noisy and ambiguous.
payload.alternatives_considered: (a) Always print "Next moves" with "  (none)". (b) Print only the closing border for terminals.
payload.why_not_alternatives: (a) misleading — there really are no follow-up commands. (b) the explanation line wouldn't be enough framing on its own.

payload.decision: Invalid `landing_state` raises `ValueError`. Call sites are internal — defensive validation, not user-facing.
payload.rationale: Closed-set states; passing anything else is a programming error. ValueError surfaces the bug at call time, in tests.
payload.alternatives_considered: (a) Silently no-op. (b) Print a generic banner. (c) Log a warning and continue.
payload.why_not_alternatives: All three hide bugs. Internal helper APIs should fail loud.

payload.decision: Wire the banner into `cmd_validate.py` only on the flat-layout `validating -> human_review` path (line 444). The staged path that lands at `followups` (line 399) does NOT print it; the followups stage's transition into `human_review` is where the staged-run banner fires.
payload.rationale: Brief AC-7 specifies this exactly. The staged path is still agent-driven (the agent owns `followups`), so it's not an agent-stopping transition.
payload.alternatives_considered: (a) Banner on both paths. (b) Banner only on staged path.
payload.why_not_alternatives: (a) would fire a STOP banner on a state the agent IS expected to drive (`followups`), diluting the signal. (b) would leave flat-layout legacy runs without a stop signal.

payload.decision: One unit-test module `tests/test_stop_banner.py` covers both the helper's behavior and the four snapshot fixtures. The E2E test extension lives in `tests/test_e2e.py`'s existing classes.
payload.rationale: Co-locating banner unit + snapshot tests keeps the change discoverable; extending the existing E2E class is consistent with how previous TODO sections have layered tests onto the happy-path scaffold.
payload.alternatives_considered: (a) Split snapshots into their own file. (b) Add new E2E class for banner.
payload.why_not_alternatives: (a) marginal benefit; the snapshot tests are tiny and tightly coupled to the unit tests. (b) the happy-path E2E already drives every relevant transition; a parallel class would duplicate setup.

payload.decision: AGENTS.md cross-reference is one paragraph inserted at the start of "How to drive the workbench" (between the heading and the existing `Run the CLI:` paragraph), not added to "Two hard rules" or to a new top-level section.
payload.rationale: Brief AC-11 calls for "one sentence" under "How to drive the workbench". Inserting it where the agent is told how to read CLI output is the right contextual home; adding a new hard rule would over-elevate a nudge.
payload.alternatives_considered: (a) Add to "Two hard rules" as rule #3. (b) Add to "When you get stuck". (c) New top-level section.
payload.why_not_alternatives: (a) the banner is a nudge, not a hard rule (per design principle "convention over enforcement"). (b) the banner is not a stuck-state recovery mechanism. (c) over-structures for a one-sentence cross-reference.
